company_name: Jiangsu Zenergy Battery Technologies Group Co., Ltd.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payment expenses' RMB31,675k (3677.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:3814); no cash taxes on equity awards disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes kpi = 0); H1 2026 run-rate RMB10.2m (interim CF statement line 1934)
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in RMB (CNY); H-share quote in HKD. fx_rate is model->quote, CNY->HKD 1.1743 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-22T11:14Z. No dual listing to parity-check: the A-share (ChiNext) listing is in tutoring and not yet priced. Per-share values are computed in RMB and multiplied by 1.1743; IPO price HK$8.27 (April 2025) is the only other HKD reference point.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-22T08:08:34Z (HKEX regular close; fifth consecutive down day, sitting on the 52-week low of 3.445 against a 52-week high of 10.43)
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,069,127,364 unlisted shares + 1,485,293,739 H shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim report, note 16 and EPS note: 'no potentially dilutive ordinary shares in issue'); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Non-SBC issuance risk is real (FY2024 RMB1.0bn general-mandate placement, FY2025 IPO RMB903m + RMB455m placement, A-share listing in tutoring) but is not modelled: a future raise is assumed to be priced at value and is covered by the bear case's funding note.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Interest-bearing bank and other borrowings 2,363.230 current + 5,030.548 non-current = 7,393.778, plus lease liabilities 30.176 + 113.352 = 143.528 (lease treatment A), less cash and cash equivalents 4,821.806 (time deposits nil at 30 June 2026). Restricted bank balances of 1,048.728 are EXCLUDED from cash: they are margin deposits securing bank acceptance bills issued to suppliers and the company books their movement inside operating cash flow, so they are working capital, not surplus cash. Treating them as free cash would add RMB0.41/share (~HK$0.48).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8%. Cost of equity 12.0% = 1.8% + beta 1.4 x 6.5% China ERP + 1.1% small-cap/liquidity premium (HK-listed H-share, RMB7.5bn market cap, 18 months of trading history). After-tax cost of debt 3.8% (FY2025 interest paid RMB230m on average borrowings ~RMB4.85bn = 4.7% pre-tax, at a 15-20% tax rate). Target weights 75% equity / 25% debt, i.e. the structure after the capex cycle rather than today's ~50% gross-debt weighting. WACC = 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.25 x 3.8 = 9.95%, rounded to 10.0%, applied identically to all three scenarios: cyclicality, pricing pressure and the capex-execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities (RMB143.5m at 30 June 2026) are added to net debt; no lease charge inside EBITDA; D&A includes right-of-use depreciation (RMB40.6m in FY2025) and the capex line is the cash-flow statement's combined 'purchases of PP&E, right-of-use assets and other intangibles', so ROU renewal is already in capex. Lease cash (RMB39.4m principal + RMB8.3m interest in FY2025) is ~0.6% of revenue, so the choice is not material; lease_cost_pct_path is 0 in every scenario.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required: the group has no non-controlling interests (total equity RMB8,473.6m is entirely attributable to owners of the parent at 30 June 2026).
inputs.jv_treatment: The 50%-owned STAES joint venture (HEV batteries for Toyota-affiliated JV OEMs) is equity-accounted: its share of profit (RMB359.9m FY2025, RMB169.6m H1 2026) sits below EBIT and its dividends (RMB295.6m FY2025, RMB347.0m H1 2026) sit in INVESTING cash flow, so neither is in reported OCF/FCF. The EBITDA margin path below is therefore the CORE ex-JV, ex-interest-income margin (FY2025: 13.6% statutory, 16.6% before the RMB235.8m PP&E impairment; H1 2026: 12.5%), and the JV is added in the equity bridge at its audited carrying value of RMB3,291.2m, which is ~9.1x FY2025 attributable JV profit and ~9.4x trailing dividends. Matching-asset rule: income stripped, asset added, once.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (10-year explicit build, end-of-year discounting), scenario-weighted, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the adaptations file applied (CNY WACC, CNY->HKD bridge, leases as debt, JV matching-asset, SBC visible but immaterial). FY0 is FY2025 (last completed December year); year 1 is FY2026, which is ~80% elapsed at the valuation date, so the house end-of-year convention discounts the whole stream ~0.8 years more than strictly necessary, worth roughly +8% to EV if adjusted; left as is for cross-ticker comparability. The pivot's EBITDA (PBT + finance costs + D&A) INCLUDES the JV share of profit, interest income and the FY2025 PP&E impairment; the margin paths here strip all three. Owner FCF base: reported FCF -1,163.8 (OCF 1,437.0 - capex 2,600.9) - SBC 31.7 - interest income 31.3 = -1,226.8. Interest income is stripped because the RMB4.8bn gross cash pile is already in the net-debt bridge. Buybacks: none ever; the flat count is a modelling convention, not something the company has paid for. This is a high-uncertainty, early-profitability name: FY2025 was the first materially profitable year, cash taxes are ~nil on recognised losses and the 15% HNTE rate, free cash flow is negative through at least FY2027 on a debt-funded capacity doubling (35.5 -> 70.5 GWh in 2026, 120 GWh targeted for 2027, RMB2.7bn of capital commitments at June 2026), and the H1 2026 gross margin compressed to 12.5% from 17.9%. The model funds the FY2026-FY2028 cash burn with the existing cash pile and borrowings at the modelled cost of debt; a discounted equity raise would transfer value from existing holders and is not modelled.

equity_bridge.item: Investments in joint ventures (STAES 50%) at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 interim note 12: share of net assets 409.0 + goodwill on acquisition 2,882.2; ~9.1x FY2025 share of JV profit (359.9), ~9.4x trailing dividends. JV income is excluded from the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Financial assets at FVTPL (bank wealth-management products)
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 balance sheet; investment income from these is excluded from the flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 5-year forward revenue CAGR (FY2025 8,101 -> FY2030 21,443). The company listed in April 2025 and core_metrics holds only FY2023-FY2025 annuals: a 2-year revenue CAGR of 39.5% (4,161.7 -> 8,101.0) and a 2-year equity CAGR of 30.6% (4,747.2 -> 8,091.8) that is mostly IPO and placement proceeds (RMB2.36bn raised FY2024-25), not retained earnings. EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: EPS was negative in FY2023 (-0.26) and FY2024 H1, and owner FCF has been negative in every period on record (FY2024 -1,045, FY2025 -1,227).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (30.6%) and revenue CAGR (39.5%) both reflect capital raised and a loss-to-profit turnaround, not a steady-state growth rate; neither is usable as a forward growth anchor. The equity CAGR is overstated by ~RMB2.36bn of new equity. Owner-FCF 'growth' is meaningless from a negative base.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is immaterial (0.4% of revenue FY2025, 0.2% H1 2026); the owner-FCF series differs from reported FCF only by SBC and interest income (~RMB60m/yr) and the sign and scale of the gap (negative FCF on a capex supercycle) is the finding, not the CAGR.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +55%: H1 2026 was +71.4% on a 39%-of-year seasonal base and capacity doubles to 70.5 GWh, but China NEV growth has slowed to +7% and pricing is deflating, so H2 decelerates. FY2027 +25% as the 120 GWh target and ESS 'second curve' ramp at partial utilisation; then fades to 3% by FY2034 as the installed-capacity ranking stabilises around 5th-7th. Year-10 revenue RMB26.3bn is ~80 GWh shipped at ~RMB0.33/Wh, well inside 2027 nameplate.
base.margin_rationale: Core ex-JV EBITDA margin anchored to H1 2026's 12.5% (the FY2025 13.6% statutory / 16.6% pre-impairment is not repeated while gross margin is 12.5%), recovering 0.5pp/yr to 15% by FY2032 as new lines absorb fixed cost and ESS/sodium-ion mix rises. Implied EBIT margin ~8% at maturity vs 7.2% FY2025 and 4.5% H1 2026. CATL runs 20%+, EVE ~15%, Gotion ~10%.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 32% of revenue (H1 actual 36%; RMB2.7bn committed at June on top of RMB1.97bn spent) and FY2027 25% for the 120 GWh target and the 20 GWh ESS line, then normalising to ~7% (D&A 6.5% plus modest growth capex) once the 2026-27 build is absorbed. The 50 GWh ESS 'intention agreement' is treated as only partly built in base.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax was RMB0.3m in FY2025 on RMB609m PBT (recognition of previously unrecognised losses -224.7m, HNTE 15% rate -42.7m, R&D super-deduction -58.3m). Ramps 2% -> 15% by FY2029 as recognised losses are consumed, then drifts to 18% from FY2032 to hedge non-renewal of the HNTE certificate (currently valid 2025-2027) against the 25% statutory rate.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer with negative working capital (trade and bills payables 7.5bn vs receivables 2.8bn + inventories 2.4bn): supplier financing via bank acceptance bills has funded growth so far (FY2025 net WC ~neutral on +58% revenue). Supplier stretch is not infinitely extendable and restricted-balance margin deposits grow with bills issued, so growth is modelled to consume 5% of incremental revenue.

bull.rationale: ESS (H1 2026 +799% YoY), sodium-ion exports and the eVTOL/robotics niches become a genuine second curve, the 120 GWh 2027 capacity fills at the 5th-ranked share, mix lifts core EBITDA to 17% (EVE-plus, still below CATL), HNTE 15% rate renewed indefinitely, and the A-share listing funds the 50 GWh ESS project at value. Capex stays elevated longer (28% FY2027) because the growth is real.

bear.rationale: FY2026 still lands +50% (H1 is already booked) but the H1 2026 margin compression is structural: CATL/BYD price to fill their own 1,000+ GWh, the 70.5 GWh is under-utilised (D&A 8% of revenue), core EBITDA settles at 10.5-12%, ESS stays sub-scale, growth stalls at 3% from FY2029. Management halts the 50 GWh project and cuts FY2027 capex to 15% to protect the balance sheet. HNTE not renewed (20% cash tax from FY2031). Supplier financing tightens (WC -8%). Value sits almost entirely in the JV stake and the terminal is capped at 12x.

scenario_narratives.base: Zenergy holds its 5th-7th place in China by installed capacity, fills most of the 2026-27 capacity doubling, and the ESS and sodium-ion lines grow from 5% of revenue to a meaningful minority. Core EBITDA margin recovers from H1 2026's 12.5% to 15% by FY2032 as the new Changshu lines absorb fixed cost; EBIT margin reaches ~8%, the ceiling for a mid-tier cell maker without CATL's purchasing scale. Free cash flow is negative through FY2028 (cumulative ~RMB5.4bn burn, funded by the RMB4.8bn cash pile and borrowings), turns positive in FY2029 and reaches ~RMB1.6bn (6% of revenue) by FY2035. The STAES HEV joint venture keeps paying ~RMB300-350m/yr of dividends and is carried at book. The axes that decide this case are (1) whether gross margin stabilises above 12% while CATL/BYD keep pricing for share, (2) utilisation of the 70.5 -> 120 GWh capacity against a Chinese NEV market growing single digits, and (3) whether the FY2026-27 capex is the last big wave or the first of several.
scenario_narratives.bull: The ESS 'second growth curve' delivers: 314Ah/588Ah cells win AIDC and long-duration storage projects, sodium-ion exports to EU/US data centres scale, and the aviation/robotics certifications become real revenue, so the 120 GWh FY2027 capacity fills at the 5th-ranked share. Mix lifts core EBITDA to 17%, the A-share ChiNext listing funds the 50 GWh ESS project without a discounted raise, and the HNTE 15% rate is renewed through the horizon. Year-10 revenue RMB35bn with ~RMB2.9bn of owner FCF; terminal capped at 15x. This case needs three independent things to go right at once (ESS scale, margin recovery, A-share funding), which is why its weight is below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: The H1 2026 gross-margin fall to 12.5% is the industry's overcapacity arriving at the mid-tier: CATL and BYD price to fill 1,000+ GWh, OEMs dual-source, and Zenergy's new 70.5 GWh runs at 60-70% utilisation. Core EBITDA settles at 10.5-12% with D&A at 8% of revenue, EBIT margin ~3-5%, growth stalls at 3% from FY2029 and the 50 GWh ESS project is shelved. Cash tax rises to 20% when the HNTE certificate lapses in 2027. Negative FCF through FY2028 on RMB7.4bn of borrowings forces either a discounted equity raise or a halt to growth capex; the model assumes the halt. The DCF equity is then little more than the STAES stake plus a low-single-digit-multiple on a thin cash flow. A receivables event at a stressed emerging-OEM customer (WM Motor precedent; RMB632m of impairment already provided) would push this case lower still.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: FY2025 was the first materially profitable year after three loss-making ones, owner FCF is negative in every period on record and stays negative through FY2028 on a debt-funded capacity doubling (borrowings RMB4.0bn -> 7.4bn in 18 months, RMB2.7bn more committed), gross margin just compressed 5.4pp, and the company is 5th-7th in a market where the top two set prices. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs ESS scale, margin recovery and A-share funding to all land together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A thin-margin, capital-intensive Chinese battery maker that has just turned profitable, is doubling capacity on borrowed money, and sits 5th-7th behind two price-setters. Value comes from three things, in order of certainty: the STAES HEV joint venture (carried at ~9x earnings, roughly RMB1.3/share before debt), a core battery business whose owner FCF is negative until FY2029, and growth optionality in ESS, sodium-ion and aviation cells that is real but small. The house DCF charges SBC (immaterial here), strips JV and interest income into the bridge, treats leases as debt, ramps cash tax from ~nil to 15-18%, charges working capital on growth, caps the terminal at 12-15x FCF for a cyclical, and discounts in CNY at 10%. Scenario spread is very wide (bear near the JV-only floor, bull ~2x price) because the business has essentially no steady-state history to anchor to.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin: every 1pp of terminal core EBITDA margin is worth roughly RMB0.25/share (~HK$0.30); H1 2026's 12.5% is the anchor and the industry has not finished cutting prices.
Capex and funding: FY2026-27 capex of ~RMB8bn is debt-funded; a discounted equity raise (A-share or H-share placement) would transfer value from existing holders and is not modelled.
Utilisation of 70.5 -> 120 GWh capacity against +7% Chinese NEV growth; under-utilisation lifts D&A % and crushes a 4-8% EBIT margin.
Cash tax: the model assumes recognised losses are consumed by FY2029 and the HNTE 15% rate (valid to 2027) is renewed; both are assumptions, not disclosures.
JV at carrying value: RMB2.9bn of the RMB3.3bn is acquisition goodwill; an impairment or a Toyota HEV volume decline would hit the bridge directly.
Receivables: RMB632m of impairment already provided; emerging-OEM customers have failed before (WM Motor).
FX and currency of valuation: a 5% CNY/HKD move shifts every HKD figure 5%; the rate is dated 2026-10-22 and refresh_price.py does not update it.
Discounting convention: FY2026 is 80% elapsed but discounted a full year; adjusting for that would add ~8% to EV.
